record.original_question: Determine whether deterministic chaos in discrete-time dynamical systems can be described in terms of Chaitin complexity, and clarify how Chaitin complexity relates to the usual definition of chaos via sensitivity to initial conditions, topological transitivity, and density of periodic points.

evidence.quote: 10. Is it possible to describe the "deterministic chaos" by means of Chaitin complexity? Discrete-time dynamical systems are called "chaotic" if they are sensitive to initial conditions. What is the relation between this definition (using topological transitivity and density of periodic points) and Chaitin complexity? (F. Geurts)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a compact metric space and $f: X \to X$ a continuous map, giving a discrete-time dynamical system $(X,f)$. Recall that $(X,f)$ is said to be chaotic in the sense of Devaney if it satisfies the following three conditions: (i) sensitive dependence on initial conditions, i.e., there exists $\delta > 0$ such that for every $x \in X$ and every neighborhood $U$ of $x$ there exist $y \in U$ and $n \geq 0$ with $d(f^n(x), f^n(y)) > \delta$; (ii) topological transitivity, i.e., for every pair of nonempty open sets $U,V \subseteq X$ there exists $n \geq 0$ with $f^n(U) \cap V \neq \emptyset$; and (iii) the set of periodic points of $f$ is dense in $X$.

Recall further that the Chaitin (Kolmogorov–Chaitin) complexity $K(s)$ of a finite binary string $s$ is the length of a shortest self-delimiting program that, when run on a fixed universal prefix-free Turing machine, outputs $s$ and halts. For an infinite binary sequence $\omega$, one studies the asymptotic behavior of $K(\omega \restriction n)$ where $\omega \restriction n$ denotes the first $n$ bits.

Problem: Provide a characterization of deterministic chaos for discrete-time dynamical systems $(X,f)$ purely in terms of the Chaitin complexity of symbolic itineraries (or, more generally, finite-precision orbit codings) generated by $f$. In particular, determine precisely the relationship between the conjunction of Devaney's three conditions (sensitivity, topological transitivity, density of periodic points) and quantitative growth properties of the Chaitin complexity $K$ along orbits of $f$, and decide whether chaos in this sense is equivalent to, implied by, or independent of suitable algorithmic-complexity conditions on these orbit codings.
artifact.status_search_result: There is a substantial literature relating Kolmogorov–Chaitin complexity of orbit codings to dynamical entropy and to various notions of chaos (e.g., works by Brudno, White, Galatolo, Bonanno, and others establishing that for sufficiently regular systems the algorithmic complexity rate of typical orbits equals the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy). However, a definitive characterization equating Devaney chaos (sensitivity + transitivity + dense periodic points) with a precise Chaitin-complexity condition does not appear to be established in full generality. The status of this specific question is therefore best classified as unknown / partially addressed by entropy-complexity correspondences but not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Kolmogorov complexity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In algorithmic information theory, the Kolmogorov complexity of an object is the length of a shortest computer program that produces the object as output; also known as Solomonoff–Kolmogorov–Chaitin complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Defines Chaitin/Kolmogorov complexity used in the problem statement.

status_evidence.title: Chaos theory - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Chaos theory focuses on underlying patterns and deterministic laws of dynamical systems highly sensitive to initial conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the standard Devaney-style components of deterministic chaos referenced in the problem.
